opening_message:
Ticket 1: Mary Lee (employee ID E015) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E015.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst. Admin exceeds the allowed maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015), full-time Analyst, requests admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; as an Analyst (full-time), the maximum allowed is write, not admin. Admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 3 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; as an Analyst, admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max is write, so admin exceeds the maximum. Recommend granting write.
Note 4 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst. As full-time employee whose role does not own the system, maximum allowed is write. Admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 5 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Mary Lee (E015) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst. As a full-time employee whose role does not own the system, the maximum allowed is write. Admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 6 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4, note 5)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB record for E015 (Mary Lee) shows employment type: contractor, security training: basic. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, so recommend granting read. Note: this differs from earlier notes that listed her as full-time; Security DB is the source for employment type and training.
reason: Mary Lee (E015) requested admin access to Source Code, which is owned by the Engineer role. The Security DB (the source for employment type and security training) records her as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Since admin exceeds the maximum of read for a contractor without advanced training, the maximum (read) is granted.

Employee: Mary Lee (E015)
Request: admin access to Source Code

- Note 6 (Security): employment type: contractor, security training: basic. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Recommendation: read. Security DB is the source for employment type and training.

So there's a conflict: Notes 1-5 say full_time, note 6 says contractor. Security's note claims the Security DB is the source for employment type and training, and it looked up in own database.

What's the policy?
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code, so max is write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

In either case, admin is above the maximum. The requested level is admin, above max, so grant the maximum.

If full-time: max = write.
If contractor: max = read (basic training).

Which is correct? The security note says employment type contractor with basic training. But the other 5 notes say full-time. Hmm.

The notes are from different agents with different databases. The security DB is described as the source for employment type and training in note 6. But note 1 says employment type looked up in own database. Note 2 says "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" - meaning it copied from note 1.

So actually note 1 looked up employment type. Note 6 (Security) also looked up employment type and found contractor. There's a conflict between note 1 and note 6.

Hmm, this is a classic inconsistency. Which one to trust? The Security agent typically is authoritative for security training and employment type? Actually, the note says "Security DB is the source for employment type and training."

Notes 2-5: some looked up, some not.

Note 6 (Security): security training basic, employment type contractor, looked up.

The question is which employment type to use. The policy difference matters: full-time → write max; contractor with basic → read max.

The Security DB says contractor, basic training. But other notes say full-time. Hmm.
